text: Time to build the shape we've been describing. Here's exactly what breaks without a relationship — and exactly how to fix it.
Priority and Hours, from two different tables. Every row shows 256 — the grand total, repeated. Power BI has no relationship telling it which hours belong to which priority.

Fix it from the Modeling ribbon: Manage relationships, New. Pick a table and column on one side, the matching table and column on the other — the column names don't need to match, just the values inside them.
Same visual, same two tables — now split correctly: 31, 77, 148. That's the entire payoff of a relationship: it gives Power BI a path to carry a filter from one table into another.

And relationships aren't fixed once created. Open Edit relationship any time — from Manage relationships, the Properties pane, or by double-clicking the line in Model view — to change how it behaves. We cover exactly what those options mean starting next lesson.
Next: cardinality — the setting that tells Power BI how many rows on each side of a relationship can match.
